summary.text: John Carter is the Republican incumbent U.S. Representative for Texas's 31st District, a lawyer and former Williamson County district judge first elected to Congress in 2002. He serves on the House Appropriations Committee and, according to his official website, chairs its Military Construction and Veterans Affairs subcommittee. He is seeking re-election in 2026.

paragraphs.text: John Carter was born in Houston, Texas, and graduated from Bellaire High School.
He earned a B.A. from Texas Tech University in 1964 and a J.D. from the University of Texas in 1969.
Carter then settled in Central Texas as a young lawyer and practiced in Round Rock; according to his official website, he was one of two lawyers in the town.
From 1981 to 2001, Carter served as judge of the 277th District Court in Williamson County; his official website says he was appointed to the bench and became known as "Judge."
He was first elected to Congress in 2002, taking office on January 3, 2003, and his official website says he decided to run after the September 11, 2001 attacks.

On the House Appropriations Committee, Carter chaired the Homeland Security subcommittee from 2013 to 2016, was ranking member of the Military Construction and Veterans Affairs subcommittee in 2021-2022, and chairs that subcommittee in the 2025-2026 session. He also sits on the Defense and Commerce, Justice, Science subcommittees.
According to his official website, he has passed legislation under Presidents Bush, Obama and Trump, including the Veterans Transplant Coverage Act on VA coverage of live-donor transplants.
Carter describes himself as a Christian (Lutheran). According to his official website, he lives in Central Texas with his wife, Erika, and they have four children and eight grandchildren.
